candidates.summary: Anthropic rebuilt its Claude Messages API from Python in Rust with Claude writing most of the code, as described by platform lead Katelyn Lesse on the Latent Space podcast; the story spread widely on X on Oct 30-31.
facts: Latent Space episode 'How Anthropic ships the #1 LLM in the World safely' with Katelyn Lesse and Angela Jiang, dated Oct 27, 2026, has a chapter 'Rebuilding the Messages API in Rust' at 56:05.
@swyx (Latent Space host) posted Oct 30: 'its true, Anthropic really vibecoded their entire backend to Rust and none of you noticed'.

Recaps of the interview on X say the team had no Rust engineers, Claude wrote the code, humans owned the plan, architecture and verification, and shadow traffic compared old and new behavior before rollout.
Recaps attribute to Lesse estimates of roughly 40-50% lower CPU use and 10-20% faster time to first token; these figures were not checked against the transcript in this run.
X news summary: 'Anthropic Rewrites Messages API in Rust Using Claude AI' was trending Oct 31.

related.name: Latent Space episode with Katelyn Lesse

candidates.summary: Stripe co-founder Patrick Collison is adding an 'improvements' box to his personal vibecoded apps: a freeform text input wired to an agent that implements whatever is submitted.
facts: Quote: 'Someone else who uses one of the applications I created has already implemented 150 improvements over the course of a few days.'
Quote: 'This pattern feels like a new kind of tool -- liquid software? -- and every application that doesn't have this feature now has a slightly rigid and anachronistic flavor.'
Open questions he lists: whether it becomes unmaintainable, how collaborative software works this way, and whether such software can be secure and reliable.
He says it 'definitely works great in a personal context' and compares it to Lisp machines, Smalltalk and HyperCard.

candidates.summary: Andrej Karpathy had Opus 5.5 build HackerTube (hackertube.org), a YouTube-style site of videos recommended in Hacker News comments, in about two hours on a Saturday.
facts: Per his post, Opus downloaded all Hacker News comments, ran Sonnet over them in a workflow to drop spam and low-grade content, and narrowed them to 40K comments recommending a YouTube video.
Result: 6,454 YouTube videos recommended on HN from 2007-2026 across 150 topics.

Features listed: 50% frame thumbnail instead of uploaded thumbnail, For You recommendations without accounts using local browser session state, keyboard shortcuts, and a data export 'to give to your agent to easily create your own version'.
He writes 'This takes ~2 hours now.'
Reached 481 points on Hacker News on Oct 31.

candidates.summary: swyx argues that a low-effort model setting plus a critique loop beats maximum reasoning effort for throughput-constrained work, pointing to his open babysit-runs skill.
facts: Post text: 'low effort + critique loop > superultramaxhighwhatever | (for the throughput-constrained; see swyxio/skills/babysit-runs)'.

The babysit-runs SKILL.md describes operating unattended runs to completion: detach runs, keep a continuation brief, schedule a temporary monitor, inspect traces and output quality, and periodically spot-check outputs with a stronger model.
The skill states 'Process health and valid schemas do not establish output quality.'

candidates.summary: @kloss_xyz says he audited 60+ agent skills across Grok Bot, Claude and Codex with Opus 5.5 on high effort and none passed as-is; he shared the grading prompt.
facts: Quote: 'I just ran this on 60+ skills across my Grok Bot, Claude, and Codex. Not a single one passed as-is.'
He says he had not audited them since setting them up a couple of months earlier.
Prompt opens: 'Grade, rank, and score every skill across our current bot setup 0-10 on triggers, correctness, learning from mistakes, ...' (post truncated in the API read).

candidates.summary: a16z's Charts of the Week says that since May average token prices are down 67% while token spend is up more than 120%.
facts: Post: 'Cheaper tokens don't mean cheaper bills. Since May: Average token prices are down 67%; Token spend is up more than 120%.'
Linked newsletter: 'Charts of the Week: Job FUD Fades' on a16z.news, which also covers the 'rack spread' (GPU prices up, token prices down).
Separate a16z post the same day quotes Moses Sternstein and Alex Danco comparing models to oil refineries and the rack spread to the refining 'crack spread'.

candidates.summary: @kunchenguid says chatting with agents is the wrong UX, based on watching his son create games: the child prefers writing, drawing and recording by hand over prompting AI.
facts: Quote: 'i'm now fully convinced that chatting with agents is absolutely the wrong UX'.
Reasons given: his son 'hates the wait and doesn't feel the result is "his work"', even though AI would give better results.
Closes with 'we need a complete rethink'.
